source.label: SYNTHETIC DEMO
source.summary: Generated illustrative intersection footage with scripted, deterministic track rows. Not a real location, real traffic, or a real incident.
source.pipeline_boundary: Scripted track rows replace YOLO + ByteTrack inference. Conflict prediction, independent incident evidence, annotated playback, human review, and the local simulated dispatch inbox run unchanged on those rows.

explanation.headline: HIGH: two vehicles were projected to reach the same point nearly together
bullets: Projected paths share a conflict point: car #1 would reach it in 0.75s and car #2 in 0.99s.
Projected footprints overlap: 0.0px apart against a 16.4px combined footprint.
The pair was closing at 252px/s in image space.
Across the observed episode, the longest consecutive run at HIGH lasted 9 frames; a minimum consecutive run is required, so a single noisy frame cannot raise this warning.
explanation.caveat: Image-space pixels and constant-velocity projection; not a measured speed, distance, or collision probability.

explanation.headline: MEDIUM: a trailing vehicle closed on a slower vehicle ahead
bullets: car #5 and car #6 travel in the same direction; the trailing vehicle is closing on the one ahead.
At constant speed their footprints would meet in about 0.46s, inside the 2.0s look-ahead window.

review_items.why_review: HIGH-priority timing; preceded a suspected collision

crossing.boundary: Crossing times are arithmetic on the assumptions entered above (distance ÷ walking speed + start-up time). They illustrate time spent in the roadway; they are not a measured crash reduction or a prediction of safety outcomes.
crossing.hypothesis: Any design change discussed here is a review hypothesis. It requires field measurement, local context, and qualified engineering review before any decision.
